senses.definition: To develop gradually over time, or change across many generations of living things.
senses.example: The design evolved as we learned what users needed.

senses.definition: A person who sings, especially as a job or in a performance.
senses.example: The singer thanked the audience after the final song.

senses.definition: To some degree, but not completely.
senses.example: The delay was partly caused by bad weather.

senses.definition: Not known, identified, or familiar to people.
senses.example: The cause of the delay is still unknown.

senses.zh: 未知事物；未知数；无名之辈
senses.definition: Something not yet known, a number to be found, or a person who is not famous.
senses.example: The actor was a complete unknown before this film.

senses.definition: A surface where customers are served, a device that counts, or a small piece used in a board game.
senses.example: Please pay at the counter near the door.

senses.definition: To reply against an argument or act to reduce an unwanted effect.
senses.example: The manager countered the criticism with new evidence.

senses.definition: Acting in the opposite direction or against another action.
senses.example: They launched a counter attack after losing ground.

senses.definition: In the opposite direction to something, often used before to.
senses.example: The new rule runs counter to our usual practice.

senses.zh: 证明…合理；为…辩护；使文字对齐
senses.definition: To show that an action is reasonable, or arrange text so its edges are even.
senses.example: The benefits do not justify the high cost.

senses.definition: Words or actions that show strong disagreement or a demand for change.
senses.example: Residents held a protest against the road closure.

senses.definition: To express strong disagreement, or state firmly that something is true.
senses.example: She protested that she had done nothing wrong.

senses.definition: A formal agreement between countries.
senses.example: The two countries signed a treaty to protect the river.

senses.definition: A serious collision, a sudden loud noise, or the sudden failure of a computer or market.
senses.example: The computer crash erased my unsaved work.

senses.definition: To hit something violently, stop working suddenly, or fall sharply in value.
senses.example: The program crashed just before I saved the file.

senses.definition: Teaching or doing a lot in a very short time.
senses.example: She took a crash course in basic Spanish before the trip.

senses.zh: 手艺；工艺；技巧；船或飞行器
senses.definition: Skill in making things, an activity using that skill, or a boat or flying vehicle.
senses.example: The market sells traditional crafts made by local people.

senses.definition: To make something carefully and skillfully.
senses.example: She crafted a clear reply to the difficult question.

senses.definition: A clear understanding of what something is really like or how it works.
senses.example: The interview gave us an insight into her work.

senses.definition: A person who uses violence and fear to pursue political or similar goals.
senses.example: The report described efforts to stop terrorist groups.

senses.definition: To own something, have a quality, or take powerful control of someone's mind.
senses.example: She possesses the patience needed for this work.

senses.zh: 轻拍；轻触；利用资源；窃听
senses.definition: To touch lightly, use a supply of something, or secretly listen to a phone line.
senses.example: Tap the screen twice to open the picture.

senses.zh: 水龙头；轻敲；轻触；电话窃听
senses.definition: A device controlling water flow, a light touch or knock, or secret listening to a phone line.
senses.example: Turn off the tap while brushing your teeth.

senses.zh: 广泛的；大规模的；大量的
senses.definition: Covering a large area or including a great amount of detail or activity.
senses.example: The storm caused extensive damage to the town.

senses.zh: 一集；一段经历；一次发作
senses.definition: One part of a series, one event in a person's life, or one period of illness or trouble.
senses.example: We watched the first episode of the new series.

senses.definition: Responsibility for something wrong, a defect, or a break in layers of rock.
senses.example: The delay was caused by an electrical fault.

senses.definition: To find something wrong with a person or their work.
senses.example: I can't fault the staff for their effort.

author: vocab_author_b

senses.definition: To become tired or make someone tired, or lose interest in something.
senses.example: The long walk tired the children.

senses.definition: The rubber covering around a wheel that touches the road.
senses.example: We had to stop and change a flat tire.

notes: 删除误导的头饰旧义，补全疲倦动词；轮胎的英式拼写为 tyre。

senses.zh: 松动的；宽松的；未捆住的；不严密的
senses.definition: Not firmly fixed, fitting tightly, tied up, or carefully controlled.
senses.example: This screw is loose and needs tightening.

senses.definition: Without being tightly fixed or held in place.
senses.example: She wore her hair hanging loose down her back.

senses.definition: To set something free or send it out suddenly.
senses.example: The archer loosed an arrow at the target.

senses.zh: 不久；很快；简短而不耐烦地
senses.definition: Soon, after a short time, or in a brief and unfriendly way.
senses.example: The train will be arriving shortly.

senses.definition: Large enough in size, amount, or importance to be noticed.
senses.example: Learning a new language takes considerable effort.

senses.definition: Existing or happening before another event, or taking priority over it.
senses.example: No prior experience is needed for the class.

senses.zh: 小隐修院院长；副院长（宗教职务）
senses.definition: A man who leads some Christian religious communities or serves just below their highest leader.
senses.example: The prior welcomed visitors to the monastery.

senses.zh: 智力的；思想的；重视理性的
senses.definition: Connected with thinking, understanding, and serious study rather than physical action.
senses.example: The course offers a real intellectual challenge.

senses.zh: 知识分子；善于思考的人
senses.definition: A person who studies and discusses ideas seriously, often as part of public life.
senses.example: The debate brought together writers and intellectuals.

senses.definition: To be a typical feature of something, or describe what someone or something is like.
senses.example: Clear speech and careful listening characterize her teaching.

senses.definition: A violent physical attack or a strong attempt to damage or defeat something.
senses.example: The police are investigating an assault near the station.

senses.definition: To attack someone physically or overwhelm their senses with something unpleasant.
senses.example: The guard was assaulted outside the building.

senses.definition: To become less tense, rest, or make a rule or control less strict.
senses.example: Try to relax your shoulders before you begin.

senses.definition: An exciting or unusual experience, often involving some risk.
senses.example: Our first camping trip turned into quite an adventure.

senses.zh: 一级台阶；楼梯（通常用 stairs）
senses.definition: One step in a set leading up or down; stairs means the whole set.
senses.example: She sat on the bottom stair to tie her shoes.

senses.zh: 外部的；来自外界的；对外的
senses.definition: On the outside, coming from outside an organization, or related to other countries.
senses.example: The project needs support from external partners.

原库以外部、外面名词解释作为唯一主条，漏掉现代常用形容词。externals 的外表细节等少见名词用法不进入本学习卡。

evidence.note: 核对外部、来自组织外、外界及对外的形容词义；自编释义与例句。

senses.definition: Facts that establish truth, a logical demonstration, a page checked before printing, or a measure of alcohol strength.
senses.example: Do you have proof that the payment was made?

senses.definition: Able to resist or remain unaffected by something, often followed by against.
senses.example: No lock is completely proof against a determined thief.

senses.zh: 校对；使面团发酵；做防护处理
senses.definition: To check text for errors, let bread dough rise, or treat something so it resists damage.
senses.example: Leave the dough to proof in a warm place.

senses.definition: Sure about your ability or about what will happen.
senses.example: She feels confident about giving the presentation.

senses.definition: The main office or center from which an organization is controlled.
senses.example: The company's headquarters are in Shanghai.

senses.definition: Happening quickly and without warning.
senses.example: A sudden noise woke the baby.

senses.definition: An act that breaks a rule, agreement, or someone's rights.
senses.example: Parking here is a violation of the rules.

senses.definition: The moving part inside the mouth used in tasting and speaking, a language, or a flap in a shoe.
senses.example: Spanish is her mother tongue.

author: vocab_author_b

senses.definition: Official permission or its document, or freedom to act beyond usual limits.
senses.example: You need a license to drive a car.

senses.definition: To give official permission for an activity or the use of something.
senses.example: The company licenses its software to schools.

notes: 美式名词和动词都可拼 license；英式名词通常 licence，动词 license。

senses.definition: Protection from danger or weather, or a place that provides it.
senses.example: We found shelter from the rain under a large tree.

senses.definition: To protect someone or something from danger or weather, or find protection yourself.
senses.example: They sheltered in the doorway until the storm passed.

senses.definition: To move something against a surface with pressure, often to clean it or spread a substance.
senses.example: Rub a little oil into the wooden handle.

senses.zh: 擦拭；按摩；难处；调味擦料
senses.definition: An act of rubbing, a mixture rubbed on food, or the main difficulty in a situation.
senses.example: Give the glass a quick rub with a soft cloth.

senses.definition: Strong public disagreement about a subject.
senses.example: The new parking rules caused a lot of controversy.

senses.zh: 入口；进入；入学或入场资格
senses.definition: A place used to go in, the act of going in, or permission to join or enter.
senses.example: Let's meet at the main entrance to the museum.

senses.definition: To hold someone's attention so completely that they notice little else.
senses.example: The children were entranced by the puppet show.

senses.definition: In the correct or suitable way, or fully and completely.
senses.example: Check that the door is properly closed.

senses.zh: 褪色；逐渐消失；逐渐减弱
senses.definition: To gradually lose color, strength, sound, or clear form.
senses.example: The photograph has faded in the sunlight.

senses.definition: An event causing great suffering, or a serious story that ends badly for its main characters.
senses.example: The fire was a tragedy for the whole community.

senses.definition: A material made of connected strings, a frame covered with it, or informally the internet.
senses.example: The ball hit the net and dropped to the ground.

senses.definition: Remaining after costs or other amounts are removed, or showing the overall result.
senses.example: The firm's net profit increased this year.

senses.definition: To catch in a net or obtain something, especially profit after costs.
senses.example: The sale netted them enough money for the trip.

senses.definition: A ceremony held after someone dies, usually before burial or burning of the body.
senses.example: Friends and family gathered for the funeral.

senses.zh: 职业；某行业全体人员；公开声明
senses.definition: A job needing special training, all people doing that work, or an open statement of belief or feeling.
senses.example: She chose teaching as her profession.

senses.definition: To form part or all of something, count as a particular thing, or formally set up an organization.
senses.example: Children constitute a large share of the visitors.

senses.definition: To make something different without replacing it completely.
senses.example: We altered our plans when the weather changed.

senses.definition: The act of setting something up, a business or institution, or the people who hold power in society.
senses.example: This family-run establishment has served meals for decades.

senses.definition: To press firmly, fit into a small space, or obtain something with difficulty or pressure.
senses.example: Squeeze the lemon over the salad.

senses.definition: An act of pressing, a situation with little room, or pressure caused by too little money.
senses.example: It was a tight squeeze to fit everyone into the car.

senses.definition: The ability to form ideas or pictures of things not present or real.
senses.example: The story captured the children's imagination.

senses.definition: A covering for the face, or something that hides a person's true feelings or intentions.
senses.example: Wear a mask when working in a dusty room.

senses.definition: To hide or cover something so it is not easily noticed.
senses.example: The music masked the noise from the street.

senses.definition: To change something into another form or use, or cause someone to adopt a new belief.
senses.example: They converted the garage into a small office.

senses.zh: 改信者；转而支持某事的人
senses.definition: Someone who has changed their religion, beliefs, or preference.
senses.example: I used to dislike cycling, but now I'm a convert.

senses.definition: Including all or nearly all the important parts of a subject.
senses.example: The guide provides comprehensive information about local transport.

senses.definition: A British secondary school that accepts pupils of different levels of ability.
senses.example: Both children attend the local comprehensive.

senses.zh: 重要知名的；显眼的；突出的
senses.definition: Important and well known, easy to notice, or sticking out from a surface.
senses.example: The notice was placed in a prominent position.

senses.zh: 演示；报告；呈现方式；颁发
senses.definition: A talk explaining something, the way it is shown, or the formal giving of a prize or gift.
senses.example: She gave a short presentation on the new design.

author: vocab_author_b

senses.zh: 无论如何；不顾；不加理会地
senses.definition: Despite a problem or what has just been said; with of, without being affected by something.
senses.example: It was raining, but they continued the game regardless.

原库中文不管、不顾为现代副词用法，旧形容词heedless类义不作为常用学习义；regardless of 为短语结构。

notes: 主词性由 adj. 改为 adv.；Cambridge 正文访问403，本轮不将搜索标题当作已核实的义项证据。

senses.zh: 负载；一批货物；负担；大量
senses.definition: An amount carried at one time, work or weight to support, or informally a large amount.
senses.example: The washing machine can handle a large load.

senses.definition: To put things into a vehicle or machine, or bring computer data into use.
senses.example: We loaded the bags into the car.

senses.definition: Not likely to change suddenly, fall, or become worse.
senses.example: The patient is now in a stable condition.

senses.zh: 马厩；同一组织的一批人或产品
senses.definition: A building where horses are kept, or a group of people or products managed together.
senses.example: The horses stayed in the stable during the storm.

senses.definition: To keep a horse in a building designed for horses.
senses.example: They stable the horses near the training field.

senses.definition: The act of presenting someone or bringing something into use, or the opening part of a text or talk.
senses.example: The book's introduction explains its main purpose.

senses.definition: To act as if something is true when you know it is not.
senses.example: The children pretended to run a restaurant.

senses.definition: Not real, but used or imagined in a game.
senses.example: She served pretend tea to her dolls.

senses.definition: Old, especially when used politely to describe adults in later life.
senses.example: He helps his elderly neighbor carry groceries.

senses.definition: Acting or speaking for others, a picture or description, or a formal statement asking for action.
senses.example: The workers asked for representation in the talks.

senses.definition: To break a law or agreement, fail to respect rights, or damage something held sacred.
senses.example: The company was fined for violating safety rules.

senses.definition: To divide into parts, break along a line, share a cost, or separate because of disagreement.
senses.example: We split the bill equally after dinner.

senses.definition: A crack or separation, a division between people or shares, or a position with the legs far apart.
senses.example: The issue caused a split within the team.

senses.definition: Divided into separate parts or opposing groups.
senses.example: The committee was split over the proposal.

senses.definition: A plant-eating wild animal with long legs; males of many kinds grow branching horns called antlers.
senses.example: We saw three deer near the edge of the forest.

senses.definition: Harmful substances or unwanted effects introduced into air, water, land, or the environment.
senses.example: The city is working to reduce air pollution.

senses.definition: Not shaking or changing suddenly, continuing regularly, or calm and reliable.
senses.example: The business has seen steady growth this year.

senses.definition: To stop something shaking or changing, or help someone become calm.
senses.example: She held the rail to steady herself.

senses.definition: Without shaking or moving, often in a short instruction.
senses.example: Hold steady while I take the photo.

senses.zh: 排放；排放物；光热等的发射
senses.definition: The release of gas, light, heat, or other energy, or something released this way.
senses.example: The factory has reduced its carbon emissions.

senses.zh: 至关重要的；生命所必需的；有活力的
senses.definition: Extremely important, necessary to keep someone alive, or full of life and energy.
senses.example: Clean water is vital to good health.

senses.definition: Money received from work or the profit made by a business.
senses.example: Her monthly earnings cover the rent and food.

senses.definition: What happens to someone or something, especially when it seems beyond their control.
senses.example: The court will decide the building's fate.

author: vocab_author_b

senses.definition: An enclosed space heated for cooking or for drying and heating materials.
senses.example: Take the bread out of the oven after twenty minutes.

notes: 删除原词库子宫的生僻隐喻/俚语义，烤箱及烘炉为学习用常用义。

senses.zh: 区别；卓越；荣誉；优秀成绩
senses.definition: A difference, a quality of excellence, or an honor or high grade awarded for achievement.
senses.example: There is an important distinction between price and value.

senses.definition: One part of a larger object, group, or whole.
senses.example: The program included a short segment about gardening.

senses.definition: To divide something into separate parts or groups.
senses.example: The survey segments customers by age and shopping habits.

senses.definition: A person who writes poems.
senses.example: The poet read a new poem at the library.

senses.definition: In no place, or to no place.
senses.example: I could find my keys nowhere in the house.

author: vocab_author_b

senses.definition: Used to stress that something is small or unimportant, or that its existence alone has an effect.
senses.example: The mere thought of the exam made him nervous.

senses.zh: 小湖；池塘（英国地名或文学用语）
senses.definition: A lake or pool, mainly used in British place names or literary descriptions.
senses.example: The old map marked a small mere beyond the village.

notes: 纠正原库仅有小湖名词的主条；现代高频仅仅的形容词置顶。保留名词但明确地域/文学使用范围。

senses.definition: Making people feel eager, interested, and full of energy.
senses.example: The children found the boat trip exciting.

senses.definition: A difference or change in amount, form, or type, or a changed version of something.
senses.example: There is wide variation in house prices across the city.

senses.zh: 舒适；安慰；慰藉；便利设施
senses.definition: A feeling of ease, relief from sadness, something that gives relief, or things making life easier.
senses.example: Her kind words brought me comfort.

senses.definition: To help someone feel less sad, worried, or afraid.
senses.example: She comforted the child after his bad dream.

senses.definition: Involving deep change or supporting changes that are far from accepted ideas.
senses.example: The report called for a radical change in policy.

senses.zh: 激进分子；根式；自由基；汉字部首
senses.definition: A person seeking deep political change; in science or language, a particular basic part or sign.
senses.example: The party was divided between moderates and radicals.

senses.definition: A sweet substance made by bees, or an affectionate name for someone you love.
senses.example: She added a spoonful of honey to the tea.

senses.definition: To change to suit new conditions, or change a work into a different form.
senses.example: It took us a few weeks to adapt to the new schedule.

senses.zh: 驻外记者；通讯员；通信者
senses.definition: A reporter covering a place or subject, or a person who exchanges letters with someone.
senses.example: Our correspondent reported from the scene of the flood.

senses.definition: Having little color, being lighter than usual, or giving weak light.
senses.example: He looked pale after the long journey.

senses.definition: To lose color or seem less important when compared with something else.
senses.example: Our small problems pale beside what they have faced.

senses.definition: A person who performs, plays, or writes music, especially with skill or as a job.
senses.example: The musicians practiced together before the concert.

senses.definition: The importance of something or the meaning it has.
senses.example: She explained the significance of the new discovery.

senses.definition: A large boat, a container for liquid, or a tube carrying fluid in a living thing.
senses.example: The doctor checked for damage to the blood vessels.

senses.definition: The act of keeping things for later use, or the space available for doing this.
senses.example: The apartment has very little storage space.

senses.definition: To leave a place quickly because of danger or fear.
senses.example: The family fled their home when the fire spread.

senses.definition: Animal skin that has been treated to make a strong material for shoes, bags, and other goods.
senses.example: The bag is made of soft brown leather.

senses.definition: To give things to several people, spread them over an area, or supply them to shops or users.
senses.example: Volunteers distributed blankets to the families.

senses.definition: Gradual change over time, including changes in living things across many generations.
senses.example: The exhibition traces the evolution of the bicycle.

senses.definition: A flat board for holding things, or a flat ledge of land below or beside the sea.
senses.example: Put the books back on the top shelf.

senses.zh: 部落；族群；一群人（非正式）
senses.definition: A social group linked by shared culture and family history, or informally a large group of similar people.
senses.example: The museum worked with members of the tribe on the exhibition.

author: vocab_author_b

senses.definition: The father of your mother or father.
senses.example: My grandfather taught me how to grow tomatoes.

senses.zh: 使继续享有旧有权利或豁免
senses.definition: To let an existing person or arrangement keep rights when new rules are introduced, usually with in.
senses.example: Existing members were grandfathered in under the old rules.

notes: 家庭关系补全外祖父；动词为制度保留旧资格而非祖父本义。

senses.definition: An area of short, regularly cut grass, or a thin smooth cotton cloth.
senses.example: The children played on the lawn after lunch.

senses.definition: The ability to make good judgments using experience and knowledge, or useful ideas gained this way.
senses.example: She questioned the wisdom of leaving so late.

senses.zh: 易受伤害的；脆弱的；易受攻击的
senses.definition: Easily hurt or harmed because of limited protection, strength, or support.
senses.example: Small plants are vulnerable to frost.
